motivation: Test finite-time electrophysiological implications with real Allen Cell Types Database Long Square recordings. This is a functional firing-rate study and does not validate spike timing, cell biophysics, instantaneous neurophysiological voltage, or the firing mechanism.
data: Allen Brain Atlas RMA model EphysSweep. All Long Square rows, all pages sorted by specimen ID, sweep number and database ID. Keep Amps entries with .99-1.01 s duration and finite numeric stimulus amplitude and explicit nonnegative integer num_spikes. Treat JSON null as missing. Round converted amplitude field to nearest integer database current unit (numerically pA per Allen convention), average observed counts across replicates at the same current. A count is compared to expected count for each actual grouped pulse duration. No spike timing inference.
selection: Sort eligible specimen IDs by sha256('HCSN-FI-v1/'+decimal id). Select first 72 cells with at least 9 eligible distinct amplitudes, amplitude span >=30 in database units, and no current < -2000 or > 2000. Selection independent of magnitude or variability of observed spike count except that an explicit count must exist. Keep silent and constant cells. Data are personally calibrated to each cell. This does not test zero-shot transfer to an entirely unseen cell.
split: For each specimen, sort current levels ascending, train on both endpoints and 2/3 of the interior, hold out interior indices 2,5,8,... (%3==2). All repeated sweeps at a given amplitude stay together. Fit each model only on training counts. Common selected specimen list and fit records sealed before evaluation. These are held-out current levels in cells whose other sweeps were available.
physical: Six-bin reflecting upper-bound generator of original pinned #7149, constant drift mu=-0.2-0.15*tanh((I-centre)/width), default spread .55, three Erlang stages and mean refractory .2, cost .15, reset 1.2. Finite-pulse expected count with initially resting distribution deposited at the nominal reset-to-boundary margin and an instantaneous mass-conserving remap to stimulus boundary before CTMC advancement. Pulse duration converts to model time using one learned nonnegative clock speed per cell. A QVI numerical grid and exact augmented matrix exponentials generate a differentiable interpolated surface, checked against direct dense calculations at random points; no optional baseline subtraction in the strict physical arms. Compare fixed nominal boundary under the identical law.
comparators: Strict moving-QVI and strict fixed-boundary count predictions have three parameters each (center, width, clock). Baselines include continuous current-to-rate rectified linear (two free parameters), deterministic constant-current LIF steady rate with refractory and 3 fitted parameters, softplus (3), constant mean (1), local piecewise-linear interpolation of observed training currents (nonparametric). Secondary baseline-subtracted physical-vs-fixed readout allows a physiologic background correction: subtract expected response at training-range minimum and clamp >=0, with the same three fitted parameters. Declare this changed observed variable.
optimization: For the three-parameter smooth rate families, calibrate development-free per specimen via bounded multistart equal-weight train mean squared error on count per one-second pulse. Current scaled to per-cell training endpoints [-1,1], center [-2,2], width [.03,4]. Clock for physical .1-500 model units per second, baseline rate scale .01-2000. Deterministic fixed starts / bounded refinements. Fit objective and scales identical for paired moving/fixed variants. Report convergence/heldout errors separately.
outcomes: Primary equal-cell mean held-out MAE in spikes per near-one-second sweep. Also RMSE, lower error win/tie/loss vs fixed and LIF; median cell error; deterministic 10000 cell bootstrap CI on paired MAE. A practical QVI advantage requires >=10% lower average held-out MAE versus both the matched fixed physical law and conventional LIF, plus bootstrap interval entirely below zero for both; report all outcomes and cold data caveats.
